project.name: Prunus Mume - Personal Center
project.instruction: Continue from the current project. Do not redesign the existing home page, Header, question-bank pages, or question pages.

prerequisites: Stage 1 core learning routes and shared navigation are complete.
The existing Meiwen visual system remains the source of truth.
designContinuity: Strictly continue the established plum and burgundy palette, near-white background, white cards, thin borders, generous whitespace, restrained typography, and end-user education-product character.
Do not introduce a new design system, component library, dashboard aesthetic, or unrelated information architecture.
Reuse existing shared components and interaction patterns where practical without rewriting completed pages.
objective: Complete the signed-in user's personal workflows for favourites, contributions, daily sign-in, profile management, and public profile viewing.

routes.name: My Favourites
requirements: Show the current user's favourited questions.
Provide keyword search, tag and difficulty filters, pagination, remove-from-favourites actions, and an empty state.
Removing a favourite must update the mock list immediately.

routes.name: Submit and Manage Contributions
requirements: Create two clear areas or tabs: Submit New Question and My Contributions.
The submission form must include title, content, answer, tags, difficulty, and whether the author recommends VIP-only access.
Contribution records must show Pending Review, Approved, and Rejected states.
Support viewing, editing, and deleting mock contributions.
Require confirmation before deletion.
Show the review comment for a rejected contribution.

routes.name: Daily Sign-In
requirements: Use a monthly calendar to display sign-in records.
Show the current streak, current-month sign-in count, and today's state.
The Sign In Today action must immediately update the calendar and statistics.
Prevent duplicate sign-in after today's action is complete.
Allow year and month switching with corresponding mock records.

routes.name: My Profile
requirements: Provide profile viewing and editing for avatar, display name, bio, phone number, email, grade, work experience, and expertise direction.
Provide a separate change-password section.
Implement local avatar preview without connecting to the real upload service.
Support edit, save, cancel, validation-error, and save-success states.

routes.name: Public User Profile
requirements: Show only public information: avatar, display name, role, bio, join date, and a summary of public question banks or contributions.
Never show account name, phone number, email, or other private fields.

personalNavigation: Complete the avatar menu or personal-center navigation so users can switch between Favourites, Contributions, Daily Sign-In, and Profile.
Use a desktop side navigation only where it fits the established layout.
Provide a mobile-appropriate navigation pattern instead of copying a desktop sidebar onto a small screen.
Keep active states and route transitions consistent with the shared application navigation.
implementationConstraints: Continue using structured TypeScript mock data and genuinely interactive local state.
Do not connect to the backend in this stage.
Do not add social feeds, rankings, direct messages, admin tools, or other features outside opendesign-prompt-client.json.
Provide loading, empty, validation, error, confirmation, and success feedback where applicable.
Maintain keyboard accessibility, visible focus states, semantic markup, and appropriate ARIA labels.
Preserve and extend stable data-od-id attributes.
Support approximately 390px mobile width without horizontal scrolling.
Update affected tests to reflect the current product instead of the original starter skeleton.
acceptanceCriteria: All five routes can be opened directly and are connected through personal-center navigation.
Removing a favourite, creating or editing a contribution, signing in today, editing a profile, and previewing an avatar are interactive.
Private profile fields never appear on the public profile route.
Forms and confirmation dialogs remain usable on mobile.
The project passes TypeScript, lint, and build checks.
